title: 0.999... equals 1, exactly, not approximately
body: Let x = 0.999...; then 10x = 9.999..., and subtracting gives 9x = 9, so x = 1. The discomfort comes from reading 0.999... as a process stopping somewhere; it names the limit itself. In the real numbers there is simply no room between it and 1 for a difference to live.
source_hint: Standard real analysis (limit of geometric series)
